lines.trans: Have you not heard anything from CEO Byun's agency?
Ugh, I keep telling you I have not!
I heard earlier too that Cindy hit it off with a chaebol heir and is at some hotel in Paris.
What business does a girl with an injured leg in a cast have in Paris?!
I heard that too—they say someone spotted her on the Champs-Elysees!
Oh right, did you see what admin clerk Go Yang-mi wore today? I check every day and she never wears the same outfit twice!
Tae-ho, is this guy the only one with way too much free time? Why are you keeping track of that?!
Think about it—how can she wear clothes that pricey on an admin salary? Unless she has secret ties to the brass…
He is writing fiction again! Excuse me, could we get a fresh grill plate here?

examples.trans: A second-generation conglomerate heir, then?

examples.text: 그럼 지금 재벌 2세랑 어디 파리 특급 호텔이라도 가 있는 거 아니야?
examples.trans: Then could she be off at some luxury hotel in Paris right now with that conglomerate heir?

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

examples.text: 나도 들었어, 샹젤리제 거리에서 본 사람이 있대요!
examples.trans: I heard that too—they say someone spotted her on the Champs-Elysees!

examples.text: 파리의 샹젤리제 거리에 뭔 특급 호텔에 있다고 소문은 쫙 났는데 여기서 지금 김에 밥을 싸 먹고 앉아 있으니 참나!
examples.trans: Rumors are flying that she is at some luxury hotel in Paris, yet here she sits wrapping rice in seaweed!

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

examples.text: 생각해봐라, 행정반 월급으로 어떻게 그렇게 비싼 걸 입냐고! 이건 고위층과 모종의 관계가 있지 않고서야…
examples.trans: Think about it—how can she wear clothes that pricey on an admin salary? Unless she has secret ties to the brass…
This point about with upper management is really important.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean term for human or logical relations.

examples.trans: human relations
What is the relationship between those two?

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.

examples.text: 다리 다쳐서 깁스한 애가 무슨 파리야, 파리!
examples.trans: What business does a girl with an injured leg in a cast have in Paris?!
Let us do that (in a cast) right away.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: Used colloquially for positive or negative emphasis.
Original sense of exceeding a limit.

examples.trans: The weather is so nice today.
Don't worry too much.
Eye hurts.
Eyes are big.

examples.text: 아 진짜 돌겠네! 돈도 없고 친구는 있는데 바쁘고 다리는 그 모양이고!
examples.trans: Oh, this is driving me crazy—no money, friends who are busy, and your leg in that state!

examples.text: 그러게요. 탁 피디님이 일부러 그러신 건 아닌 거 아는데요, 다리만 좀 멀쩡했어도 상황이 훨씬 나았을 텐데.
examples.trans: Tell me about it. I know Producer Tak did not do it on purpose, yet if only my leg were fine, things would be way better.
Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.

다치다.gloss: to get hurt, to be injured

examples.trans: I fell and hurt my knee.
Be careful not to get hurt.
He is our company's president.
I will speak as the representative.
Listen well.
Listen to a song.
See you again!
It is raining again.

맞다.gloss: to be right, to be correct

meanings.note: Used to confirm facts or answers.

meanings.en: to fit, to suit, to match

examples.trans: Yes, that's my phone number.
These shoes fit my feet perfectly.

meanings.note: Used both as an adverb and a noun

examples.trans: I drink coffee every morning.
I try to exercise every day.

examples.text: 생각해봐라, 행정반 월급으로 어떻게 그렇게 비싼 걸 입냐고! 이건 고위층과 모종의 관계가 있지 않고서야…
examples.trans: Think about it—how can she wear clothes that pricey on an admin salary? Unless she has secret ties to the brass…
This point about some covert kind of is really important.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a noun in questions

examples.trans: What kind of music are you listening to right now?
Is something the matter?

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

examples.text: 얘 또 소설 쓴다! 여기 불판 좀 바꿔줘요.
examples.trans: He is writing fiction again! Excuse me, could we get a fresh grill plate here?
Let us do that (change for us) right away.

meanings.note: Used for gifts, money, messages, or documents.

examples.trans: I received a birthday present.
Please answer the phone.

meanings.note: Follows native Korean numbers (한 번, 두 번, 세 번) to count how many times.

examples.trans: I watched this movie three times.
Please explain it just one more time.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

examples.text: 얘 또 소설 쓴다! 여기 불판 좀 바꿔줘요.
examples.trans: He is writing fiction again! Excuse me, could we get a fresh grill plate here?
This point about barbecue grill plate is really important.

examples.text: 골라도 비싼 애기를 골랐어! 이 치사한 놈 진짜, 이거 손만 대봐!
examples.trans: Out of all of them, he picked an expensive baby! You petty jerk—just dare lay a finger on it!

examples.text: 생각해봐라, 행정반 월급으로 어떻게 그렇게 비싼 걸 입냐고! 이건 고위층과 모종의 관계가 있지 않고서야…
examples.trans: Think about it—how can she wear clothes that pricey on an admin salary? Unless she has secret ties to the brass…

meanings.note: Can refer to a single person or people/a crowd in general without a plural suffix.

examples.trans: There are many people in the cafeteria.
He is a good person.

examples.text: 잘 생각해보세요, 저런 여자가 의외로 진국일 수가 있다니까.
examples.trans: Give it serious thought—a woman like her can turn out to be the real deal.
This expression comes from 'think it over'.

examples.text: 얘 또 소설 쓴다! 여기 불판 좀 바꿔줘요.
examples.trans: He is writing fiction again! Excuse me, could we get a fresh grill plate here?
This point about a novel, fiction is really important.

meanings.note: Irregular ㅡ-stem verb: 쓰다 + -어 becomes 써.
Commonly used for tools, money, or time.

examples.trans: I write in my diary every night.
I wrote my name on the very first page of the book.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization, surprise, or hesitation.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Oh, I see!

meanings.en: earlier, a short while ago (same day)

examples.trans: I called earlier.
What did you say earlier?

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

examples.text: 아유 설마, 전화 좀 해 봐!
examples.trans: Oh come on, surely not—give him a call right now!
Here the word for 'oh goodness' is key.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: Auxiliary negative verb/adjective used after -지 (long-form negation)

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold today.
I didn't say anything.

meanings.note: Colloquially used to refer to people of the same age or younger.

examples.trans: Kids are running around and playing in the park.
That person has a really good personality.
This is my friend Minsu.
He/she did it all.

meanings.note: Contraction of 이 아이; used when introducing or referring to someone younger or close

examples.trans: Where is the restroom?
Where are you right now?
How did you get here?
How should we solve this problem?

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.

meanings.note: Often used directly without a locative particle to mean 'here'.

examples.trans: Please sit here.
Here is our office.

meanings.note: Used in 연락을 하다 ('to contact') and humble 연락을 드리다.

examples.trans: I will contact you later.
I heard from my friend today.

meanings.note: The present day; often used adverbially without a particle.

examples.trans: The weather is nice today.
What day of the week is it today?

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.
The outfit you're wearing today is really pretty.
It's cold, so please wear warm clothes.
I received my salary.
first paycheck
How much is this?
Please look at this.

meanings.note: Used for clothing worn on the body (shirts, pants, dresses, outfits).

examples.trans: I wore a black coat today.
It's cold, so please dress warmly.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)

meanings.note: Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

examples.trans: A second-generation conglomerate heir, then?

examples.text: 맞네! 재벌이랑 사귀니까 위약금 따위 두렵지 않다 그러고 펑크 낸 거지!
examples.trans: That has to be it! Because she is dating a tycoon, she is unafraid of penalty fees and blew off the event!
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: used to emphasize an adjective or adverb

examples.trans: The food is really delicious today.
Time really flies.

examples.text: 아 참, 오늘 행정반 고양미 입고 온 옷 봤어요? 내가 매일 체크하고 있는데 옷을 한 번도 같은 걸 안 입어요!
examples.trans: Oh right, did you see what admin clerk Go Yang-mi wore today? I check every day and she never wears the same outfit twice!

examples.text: 형, 얘만 너무 한가한 거 아니야? 뭘 그런 걸 체크하고 있냐!
examples.trans: Tae-ho, is this guy the only one with way too much free time? Why are you keeping track of that?!

meanings.note: Determiner form of 하나, used before a noun counter.

examples.trans: one person
one hour

examples.text: 형, 얘만 너무 한가한 거 아니야? 뭘 그런 걸 체크하고 있냐!
examples.trans: Tae-ho, is this guy the only one with way too much free time? Why are you keeping track of that?!
It is really idle, free compared to what I expected.

examples.text: 너네 팀이 종이 타러 가면 행정반에서 별소리 안 하고 주지?
examples.trans: When your team goes to pick up paper, the admin desk hands it over without a fuss, right?
Here the word for 'at the admin supply desk' is key.

meanings.note: Used by a younger male to address an older brother or close older male friend/colleague.

examples.trans: Hey, do you have time tonight?
My older brother is an office worker.

examples.text: 신디, 우리가 돈은 어떻게든 빌려줄 테니까 특급 호텔 같은 데 가 있는 거 어때?
examples.trans: Cindy, we will lend you the money somehow, so how about staying at a five-star hotel?

examples.text: 그럼 지금 재벌 2세랑 어디 파리 특급 호텔이라도 가 있는 거 아니야?
examples.trans: Then could she be off at some luxury hotel in Paris right now with that conglomerate heir?
